task.title: Perf measurement helper can leak its busy-loop child process
task.description: Found an orphaned busy-loop helper from TestMeasureCommandTerminatesTimedOutDescendant (sh -c 'echo $$ > "$1"; while :; do :; done') that had been running for 7 days 19 hours with PPID 1, burning ~80% of a CPU core since roughly 2026-07-30 — the date of the performance evidence collection. The test exists to assert that measure terminates timed-out descendants, yet this descendant escaped both the code under test and the test's own cleanup, so there is a gap on darwin: either the test tears down without ensuring the child is dead, or the process-group termination in the measurement harness does not reliably reach grandchildren (sh spawning the loop). Investigate process-group kill semantics (setpgid + kill of the negative pgid) and make the test's cleanup unconditionally reap the child even if the test binary dies mid-run. Besides the leak itself, a stray spinning core silently skews later perf evidence runs on the same host, which the scaling tickets care about. Observed and manually killed 2026-08-07 while monitoring v0.4.1 perf acceptance runs.
